content: This product does not guarantee safety, effectiveness, or suitability for your specific needs. The information provided here is not a substitute for personalized medical advice and should not replace the guidance of your healthcare professional. Always consult your healthcare provider for comprehensive information about this product and your individual health requirements. Uses: This medication is used in combination with other HIV treatments to help manage HIV infection. It works by reducing the amount of HIV in your body, allowing your immune system to function more effectively. However, enfuvirtide is not a cure for HIV. To minimize the risk of transmitting HIV to others, continue taking all prescribed HIV medications as directed by your doctor. Additionally, use effective barrier methods, such as latex or polyurethane condoms or dental dams, during sexual activity as instructed by your healthcare provider. Avoid sharing personal items like needles, syringes, toothbrushes, or razors that may have come into contact with blood or bodily fluids. How to Use: Before starting enfuvirtide, read the patient information leaflet and instructions for use provided by your pharmacist. Consult your healthcare provider for guidance on how to prepare and administer this medication. Enfuvirtide is injected under the skin, typically twice daily, as directed by your doctor. The injection is usually administered in the upper arm, thigh, or abdomen. Avoid injecting into the buttocks or near the elbow, knee, or groin. Inspect the medication visually for particles or discoloration before use; do not use the liquid if either is present. Clean the injection site with rubbing alcohol before each dose, and rotate injection sites to reduce the risk of skin injury. Do not inject into areas with bumps from previous injections, moles, scars, bruises, tattoos, burns, or the belly button. To reduce bruising, avoid rubbing the injection site after administration. It is crucial to continue using this medication, along with other anti-HIV treatments, exactly as prescribed by your doctor. For optimal results, administer the medication at evenly spaced intervals. Side Effects: Common side effects include pain, redness, itching, bruising, hardened skin, or bumps at the injection site, which may last up to seven days. A runny nose may also occur. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. As your immune system strengthens, it may begin to fight off pre-existing infections, potentially causing symptoms of those infections to reappear. In some cases, an overactive immune response may occur, which can happen at any time, either shortly after starting HIV treatment or months later. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for guidance. Precautions: Before using enfuvirtide, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when clearly necessary. HIV treatment can reduce the risk of transmitting the infection to your baby, and enfuvirtide may be part of that treatment. It is unknown whether this medication passes into breast milk. Drug Interactions: Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Overdose: If someone has overdosed and exhibits serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Lab Tests and Appointments: Regular lab and medical tests, such as liver function tests, should be conducted while using this medication. Missed Dose: It is important to take each dose of this medication as scheduled. If you miss a dose, contact your doctor or pharmacist immediately for a new dosing schedule. Storage: Before mixing, store the dry powder and mixing solution at room temperature. Once mixed, refrigerate the medication and use it within 24 hours. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Important Information: This summary does not include all possible information about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
